ItemStage.description: The terminal stage for an item.
ItemStage.title: ItemStage

changelog.change: Initial shape: one row per (date, stage) folded from an item-health shard.
changelog.why: The item-health census grows at about 212,000 bytes a published day and nothing bounded it. Deleting an old shard outright would answer that and cost every year-over-year comparison, so a month past observability.keep_months is folded to this shape first. Five rows a day keeps the counts and the timing distribution and drops only the per-item detail, which is what the console's failure list offers and no rate needs.

description: One `(date, stage)` pair, summarised from the item-health shard.

failed.description: Of those rows, the ones whose outcome was not ok. The numerator.
failed.title: Failed

items.description: Rows the shard held for this date and stage, counted as they were written. A run that executed twice under one run id really does leave two rows for one item, and the fold reproduces that rather than deciding for a later reader which of them to believe.
items.title: Items

max_ms.description: The slowest row of the group.
max_ms.title: Max Ms

p50_ms.description: Nearest-rank median of fetch, extract and summarize milliseconds added up per row. Empty when no row at this stage recorded any - empty is not zero.
p50_ms.title: P50 Ms

sum_ms.description: Every timed row added together, so a day's total stage time survives the fold. A percentile cannot be re-added into a total; this can.
sum_ms.title: Sum Ms

timed.description: Of those rows, the ones that recorded any milliseconds at all. The denominator the four figures below are taken over, which is never the row count: a plan-stage row times nothing, and a row written before the timing columns existed times nothing either.
timed.title: Timed
